messages:
Maya: Quick proposal — 'deploy lanes' as small named bundles for common deploy patterns. each lane = pin, change-window, canary policy, and rollback hint. idea is a single bot command to run standard ops for a feature area.
Maya: Example command sketch:
```
/deploy lane payments-canary --pin v2.3.1 --window 2026-03-25T09:00Z/2026-03-25T10:00Z --canary 5% --notify #payments-oncall --dryrun
```
Maya: Lane manifests would live in infra/deploy/lanes/*.yaml so product teams can review PRs for lane changes.
Kevin: I like it. Can lanes support multiple sequential stages (staging -> canary -> prod) with auto-promotion? :thumbsup:
Maya: Yes — lane manifest can list stages with promotion rules and observability gates. promotion can be manual or automatic when checks pass.
Sam: Where do we store the rollback target? Do we record last-green pin per-service somewhere?
Alisha: We should record the last-known-good pin in the lane state in our deploy meta DB (encrypted). rollback command should default to that. For secrets, reference existing config service (no plaintext in lane yml).
Jordan: Minimal rollback UX: `/deploy rollback --lane payments-canary --reason "latency spike"` should revert to last-green and annotate release notes. Also add `--force` for emergency revert.
Kevin: We should also surface a small checklist auto-run before promotion: smoke tests, error-rate threshold, requests/sec sanity. ops-bot can assert pass/fail.
Maya: Example lane yaml (sketch):
```yaml
name: payments-canary
stages:
  - name: staging
    pin: v2.3.1-staging
  - name: canary
    pin: v2.3.1
    canary_pct: 5
    checks:
      - name: error_rate_under_0.5%
      - name: p95_latency_under_600ms
rollbacks:
  strategy: last_green
  autopage: true
notifications:
  channel: "#payments-oncall"
  postmortem_channel: "#payments-postmortem"
```
Sam: Nice. A couple of operational notes:
- Respect change windows automatically: if now outside window, queue and notify.
- Provide a tokenized dry-run output so reviewers can see the exact infra changes.
Alisha: For security teams: add an optional `approval_requirements` field so sensitive lanes require an approver from a list (eg. @sec, @pci-owner).
Jordan: Rollback script snippet (for deploy-bot automation):
```bash
# run as part of bot action
DEPLOY_ID=$1
if /deploy status $DEPLOY_ID | grep -q "failed_checks"; then
  /deploy rollback --id $DEPLOY_ID --to last_green --message "auto-rollback: failed checks"
fi
```
Maya: UX details: bot should announce pinned version, the rollforward/rollback affordances, and attach a small release-note template on deploy start. example note:
"Deploy payments v2.3.1 — canary 5% in change window 09:00-10:00 UTC. Contact @payments-oncall for hotfixes. Rollback: /deploy rollback --lane payments-canary"
Kevin: Could we add a short `--explain` output from /deploy that prints what the bot will do step-by-step? reviewers love that.
Maya: yes — `/deploy lane ... --explain` outputs plan, diffs, and required approvals.
deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy lane 'payments-canary' (id: d-20260325-001) for 2026-03-25T09:00Z. Use `/deploy status d-20260325-001` to follow.
Jordan: One more: surface a small metric snapshot at promotion time (error rate, p95, qps) so review is faster. ops-bot can attach.
Alisha: I'll sketch a PR template and a lane schema draft. want to pair with someone on the rollout safety gates tomorrow.
Sam: Happy to pair. If we get this in place it should cut manual steps for our regular rollouts by ~40%.
Maya: Great — I'll open the repo PR with schema + deploy-bot handlers. tagging @payments team to review after initial draft.
Kevin: :rocket:
deploy-bot: Note: `/deploy rollback --lane payments-canary --to last_green` will create a revert deploy and annotate original with `reverted_by` metadata.
Maya: Thanks all — next step: PR + brief doc in release playbooks.
